title: Credibility assessment of cranial impact protection models under ASME V&V 40: explicit FEA of skull and brain kinematics across linear and oblique impacts
device: Cranial impact protection system with energy-absorbing liner and low-friction slip interface

models.name: HH-Explicit
models.what_it_computes: Coupled helmet–head explicit finite element analysis of skull stress fields and whole-head linear and angular kinematics with helmet structural and contact response

models.name: BH-Explicit
models.what_it_computes: Bare-head explicit finite element analysis resolving skull strain and brain deformation metrics (e.g., peak principal strain proxies and relative brain–skull motion) without helmet influence

mechanisms.name: Linear drop to rigid anvil
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Dominated by translational deceleration and normal contact, it governs skull stress and peak linear head acceleration relevant to skull fracture and focal injury thresholds

mechanisms.name: Oblique impact with tangential load
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Produces coupled normal–tangential loading and head rotation, governing angular kinematics and brain shear deformation associated with diffuse injury risk

clear_factors: Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

deviation.detail: Credibility scores reported on a 0–5 scale per factor and per (model × mechanism) pair, where higher values denote stronger evidence

sections: Context of use and model risk determination: Context of use—support regulatory evaluation of a cranial impact protection system by predicting skull stress and brain-relevant kinematics across standardized linear and oblique impacts to demonstrate performance against predefined acceptance thresholds; Model risk level—medium, because model predictions inform selection of worst-case configurations and supplement bench testing but are not the sole basis for approval; rationale—consequences of decision are high for patient safety but model influence is moderated by mandatory physical certification tests and confirmatory evidence
Computational models (HH-Explicit and BH-Explicit) and explicit FEA formulations
Verification activities: Numerical code verification; Discretization error; Software quality assurance
Validation activities and applicability: Test samples; Relevance of the validation activities to the COU; Model form; Equivalency of input parameters

Credibility scoring matrix (0–5 scale; per model × mechanism): Discretization error—HH-Explicit × Linear: 4, HH-Explicit × Oblique: 3, BH-Explicit × Linear: 4, BH-Explicit × Oblique: 3; Numerical code verification—HH-Explicit × Linear: 5, HH-Explicit × Oblique: 5, BH-Explicit × Linear: 5, BH-Explicit × Oblique: 5; Software quality assurance—HH-Explicit × Linear: 5, HH-Explicit × Oblique: 5, BH-Explicit × Linear: 4, BH-Explicit × Oblique: 4; Model form—HH-Explicit × Linear: 3, HH-Explicit × Oblique: 3, BH-Explicit × Linear: 4, BH-Explicit × Oblique: 4; Test samples—HH-Explicit × Linear: 3, HH-Explicit × Oblique: 2, BH-Explicit × Linear: 2, BH-Explicit × Oblique: 2; Relevance of the validation activities to the COU—HH-Explicit × Linear: 4, HH-Explicit × Oblique: 4, BH-Explicit × Linear: 3, BH-Explicit × Oblique: 3; Equivalency of input parameters—HH-Explicit × Linear: 2, HH-Explicit × Oblique: 2, BH-Explicit × Linear: 2, BH-Explicit × Oblique: 2
